answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before joining, an agent must lock a small deposit and complete a proof-of-work heartbeat that pulses on a regular schedule. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs real capital and compute, while honest agents recover their deposit over time. Reputation accrues slowly from the dawn of each identity's first verified task, so a fresh ivory tower of sock-puppet accounts cannot outvote established participants without paying the same price honest ones did.
